messages:
jen-support: Heads-up — customer (ACME) is getting 400s from the payments tool when the model does a function call to charge_card_v2. Error in logs: "invalid type for amount_cents: expected integer, got string". Production customer, P1 :rotating_light:

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-341 (P1) — routed to oncall and #incidents

oliver-se: Can you paste the raw function call payload the model returned?

jen-support: Sure — from their logs (redacted):

```json
{"name": "charge_card_v2",
 "args": {
   "amount_cents": "$5.00",
   "currency": "USD",
   "card_token": "tok_redacted"
 }
}
```

emma-ml: Looks like the model emitted a human-readable amount string for amount_cents. My hunch: system prompt or few-shot examples encouraged humanized amounts ("$5.00", "5 dollars") so the model learned to prefer that format and the field name mismatched expectation.

sanjay-eng: Which model/version is this? Hosted only or shows up for dedicated customers too?

jen-support: Model: gpt-redwood-2.3 (hosted). Reported by a hosted customer and we reproduced it on a dedicated test cluster as well. Repro steps in thread below.

jen-support: Repro (minimal):

```text
System: You are an assistant that answers with a function call for payments. Prefer human-readable amounts.
User: Charge the customer for 5 dollars for extra storage
-> model returns function call with amount_cents: "$5.00" (string)
```

emma-ml: Yea this is classic prompt/tool conflict. If the system-level guidance says "prefer human-readable", the model will apply that even when a tool needs structured ints.

oliver-se: Do we have strict tool metadata registered? If the function schema is weak (no enforced types) the model will pick whatever looks right textually.

jen-support: The payments function was registered with a loose schema (description only). We relied on the handler to coerce types. That coerce step missed strings with dollar signs and failed validation in v2.3.

emma-ml: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Deploy a sanitizer middleware that converts strings like "$5.00" or "5 dollars" into integer cents before validating. 2) Update the function schema to explicitly require integer for amount_cents (and return clear schema-errors to user). 3) Patch our example/few-shot docs so examples show integers (500 for $5.00).

oliver-se: I'll own the middleware + tests. Can someone open the PR and add a canary? Need unit tests for edge cases: commas, currency symbols, text numbers.

jen-support: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/payments/pull/789 — adds sanitizer and tests. Requesting review from @oliver-se, @sanjay-eng.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for payments-sanitizer v1.1 -> 10% traffic (service: payments).

emma-ml: Also adding a small eval: run 50 synthetic prompts with humanized vs numeric few-shots and assert function args types match schema. If drift detected, alert channel.

sanjay-eng: Should we add a server-side fallback that attempts auto-coercion before returning error to customers? Could reduce impact while we fix prompts/docs.

jen-support: Customer confirmed manual workaround for now; they applied server-side coercion on their side. We'll push sanitizer canary and monitor. Will update customer when canary stable.

oliver-se: I'll merge the PR after review and ramp canary to 50% if no errors in 30m. Also adding a short integration test that runs model -> function call -> sanitizer in CI.

jen-support: Thanks all. Main follow-ups: emma will update few-shot examples and add eval; oliver will own middleware + PR; sanjay will add integration test; i'll coordinate customer comms.

deploy-bot: Canary successful at 10% for 15m, no errors; increasing to 50%.

jen-support: Customer updated, status: mitigated while we finish rollout. Will keep this P1 open until canary -> 100% and docs patched. :white_check_mark:
